tasks.short: Administer approved assessments, score responses, and prepare results for qualified interpretation.

steps.what: Confirm the instrument, purpose, accommodations, and authorised recipients.
Register participants and send assessment instructions and appointments.
Administer the assessment and address procedural questions using the assessment platform in {OTHER}.
Calculate scores against authorised norms in the assessment platform in {OTHER}.
Assemble scores, completion checks, and administration notes into a restricted report.
Interpret limitations, discuss results, and authorise release to named recipients.
File the approved report and record restricted access and retention dates.

tasks.design: Configure the assessment platform in {OTHER} for invitations, authorised scoring, and completion checks; use a deterministic report generator to assemble results in {DOCS}. File approved results in the appropriate {ATS} or {HCM} record with restricted access and retention rules. Qualified people retain instrument selection, accommodations, interpretation, and release decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessment platforms often already score responses. The remaining friction comes from disconnected registrations, report assembly, permissions, and specialist review.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing platform configuration and small integrations can remove copying. AI-assisted coding can shorten implementation, but adds no psychometric validity.
tasks.still_hard: Instrument validity, licensing, accessibility, norm selection, and qualified interpretation remain costly. GDPR applies, and any proposed AI use in employment assessment needs EU AI Act classification; national rules may require consultation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when language, disability, context, or poor administration makes a score misleading, and explain limitations sensitively.

ambition.what: An accessible assessment preparation service with an individual accommodations check.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time assembling reports and more time preparing participants and resolving administration problems. They gain discretion to arrange approved accommodations and pause an invalid session, not to make hiring decisions.

reach.task: Check assessment administration quality before interpreting results.
reach.learn: Instrument protocols, accessibility adjustments, scoring flags, and limits of interpretation.

evidence.claim: Approved assessment scoring and fixed report assembly can use existing configuration and deterministic templates.
GDPR restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects.
Recruitment AI can fall within the EU AI Act high-risk categories; procedural exceptions require assessment.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The company uses licensed instruments with authorised scoring rules and qualified interpretation.
The assessment platform is the assessment-system category represented by {OTHER}.
The sequence shows recruitment assessments; employee development assessments connect to performance-cycle instead.
Scoring is already automated in many companies; the design claims no new saving for that existing automation.
Build ranges cover one instrument workflow and include access review and consultation work where applicable.
unknowns: Which instruments, licences, scoring methods, and export interfaces are available?
Who is qualified to interpret results and authorise disclosure?
What accommodations, lawful basis, retention periods, and recipient restrictions apply?
Which national rules and employee consultation arrangements apply?
research_questions: Can the platform generate the required report and retention controls without custom code?
Which proposed uses, if any, require an EU AI Act employment-system assessment?
new_work: Review report exceptions and administration flags.
Maintain instrument versions, norm references, and report templates.
Audit recipient permissions and deletion schedules.
Test integrations after platform or instrument changes.

tasks.short: Prepare employee badges, verify identity, arrange authorised access, and maintain badge records.

steps.what: Collect starter or replacement requests and check employee details.
Verify identity and collect or check the badge photograph.
Approve access zones and expiry in the physical access-control system in {OTHER}.
Enter approved employee details and permissions in the physical access-control system in {OTHER}.
Prepare the print layout in the badge-printing system in {OTHER}.
Load badge stock, collect the printed badge, and inspect its quality.
Match the recipient to the badge, hand it over, and explain loss procedures.
Record badge issue and expiry against the employee record.
Revoke lost, expired, or leaver badges in the physical access-control system in {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Connect approved employee events in {HCM} to the physical access-control and badge-printing systems in {OTHER}, using {WORKFLOW} for missing details and access approval. Generate print jobs, record handovers, and apply authorised expiry, loss, and leaver revocations with reconciliation logs. People verify identity, approve permissions, inspect badges, and control physical handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical issuance and security approvals obscured the smaller automation opportunity. Separate employee and access records also made duplicate entry appear unavoidable.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing badge templates, approval configuration, and deterministic connectors can remove repeated entry. AI-assisted coding can make a narrow connector cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy hardware interfaces, urgent replacements, identity discrepancies, and physical custody remain. GDPR applies to employee data; access-log uses and employee consultation depend on national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve identity discrepancies and unusual access requests, and ensure the badge reaches the right person.

ambition.what: A pre-arrival badge readiness service that resolves missing information before the employee arrives.

tasks.altitude: The assistant handles fewer duplicate entries and spends more time resolving readiness exceptions. They gain authority to return incomplete requests and arrange collection; security retains access decisions.

reach.task: Coordinate starter readiness across employee records and workplace access.
reach.learn: Effective dates, access profiles, identity procedures, and escalation paths.

evidence.claim: Employee self-service changes can feed downstream personnel processes.
Badge templates, access approvals, and event-driven revocation can use deterministic configuration and integrations.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates; the digest contains no badge-specific case.

assumptions: Badge printing and physical access-control categories are represented by {OTHER}.
Existing printing hardware remains in use.
Revocation uses authenticated loss reports, approved leaver events, or recorded expiry dates.
No facial recognition or employee behaviour scoring is introduced.
The security-related scope is badge issuance, permissions, and revocation.
Build ranges include access review and applicable consultation work; hardware replacement is excluded.
unknowns: Do the access-control and badge-printing systems support suitable interfaces?
Who approves access zones, activation, and exceptional permissions?
How are urgent loss reports authenticated and routed?
What are the employee-data retention rules and applicable national consultation requirements?
research_questions: Can existing provisioning configuration replace a custom connector?
How will failed revocations be detected and escalated promptly?
Can handover confirmation trigger activation without exposing access before collection?
new_work: Handle rejected updates, duplicate identities, and failed revocations.
Maintain access-profile mappings and badge templates.
Review permissions and test loss and leaver scenarios after changes.

tasks.short: Arrange internal and external training, including schedules, bookings, enrolments, and completion records.

steps.what: Collect training requests, participant details, and availability.
Agree learning objectives, priority, and operational cover.
Compare internal courses and external proposals against the learning brief.

loop.input: External provider proposals containing course scope, dates, fees, accessibility, and cancellation terms.
loop.output: A comparison table with source passages and explicit missing fields.
loop.check: Validate dates, currency, and totals with code; the assistant checks scope and contractual terms against sources.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per proposal; missing or conflicting fields go to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Use catalogue fields directly for internal courses. External proposals vary in wording and layout, so fixed mappings do not reliably extract their terms.

steps.what: Match dates, rooms, capacity, and participant availability in a planning workbook.
Approve the course, dates, expenditure, and booking terms.
Confirm the authorised provider booking or internal trainer reservation.
Enrol participants and send joining instructions and reminders.
Record attendance, completion evidence, and outstanding certificates.

tasks.design: Collect structured requests in {LMS} or {WORKFLOW}, and use deterministic scheduling against {CALENDAR} and course capacity. A bounded extraction loop turns varied external proposals into a source-linked comparison for review; the budget owner approves the actual booking terms in {PROCUREMENT}. Approved bookings trigger enrolments, instructions, reminders, and completion checks in {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability, provider terms, budget approval, and enrolments sit in different places. Changing dates and inconsistent proposals make mailbox coordination persist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment and approval configuration handles much of the work. Small scheduling integrations and bounded proposal extraction can now be built and tested more cheaply.
tasks.still_hard: Learning fit, operational cover, provider negotiation, accessibility, and cancellations remain human problems. GDPR applies to participant data; employee consultation under national rules may apply to new monitoring or changed data uses.
tasks.human_edge: Understand why training is needed, negotiate workable attendance, and recognise when a convenient course will not solve the learning problem.

ambition.what: A recurring training offer for shift-based employees, with sessions matched to shift availability.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time chasing replies and copying enrolments, and more time resolving access and scheduling barriers. They can propose cohort and session changes within approved budgets; managers retain learning priorities and spending approval.

reach.task: Translate a learning brief into a suitable course shortlist and practical cohort plan.
reach.learn: Learning objectives, provider evaluation, accessibility, and evidence of training effectiveness.

evidence.claim: Enrolment, reminders, capacity checks, and approval routing can usually use existing configuration or deterministic code.
Document extraction with validation and exception routing is an established pattern, though the cited capability concerns orders.
The digest provides no training-coordination case establishing these savings.
Time shares, remaining effort, and build ranges are planning estimates for a limited initial rollout.

assumptions: The company has an {LMS}, shared calendars, and an established booking approval process.
A planning workbook currently bridges availability and course options.
Routine bookings can be sent using approved templates and exact authorised terms.
Changed prices, dates, or cancellation terms require renewed approval before commitment.
Completion imports require trustworthy attendance evidence; enrolment alone does not establish completion.
Build ranges include access review and applicable consultation work, not a full learning-system replacement.
unknowns: Which enrolment, calendar, procurement, and attendance interfaces are available?
How often do providers require negotiation or portal-only booking?
Who approves learning suitability, expenditure, and changed booking terms?
Which shift, accessibility, language, and operational-cover constraints must scheduling respect?
Do proposed data uses trigger consultation under applicable national rules?
research_questions: Can existing {LMS} scheduling and enrolment features cover the initial scope?
Which proposal fields need source checks before booking approval?
Can providers supply structured attendance files to avoid another extraction loop?
new_work: Review extracted proposal terms and unsupported scheduling constraints.
Handle booking changes and renewed approvals.
Maintain course metadata, calendars, booking templates, and extraction checks.
Resolve missing attendance evidence and certificates.
Check whether shift-based employees can actually attend the sessions offered.

role.altitude: The assistant shifts from copying records and chasing coordination to preparing reliable cases, resolving exceptions, and supporting employees. New discretion concerns readiness, scheduling proposals, and procedural escalation; assessment interpretation, access permissions, and spending remain with authorised roles.
reach: HR specialist: assessment administration quality and starter readiness.
Training and development specialist: course suitability and accessible cohort planning.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, approvals, permissions, and retention rules.
Map employee identifiers and reconcile records across systems.
Check source evidence, scoring flags, and extracted contractual terms.
Understand assessment protocols, accessibility, and escalation boundaries.
Translate learning needs into practical scheduling constraints.
role.ambitious_version: Run an employee readiness service spanning assessment preparation, workplace access, and accessible training, with clear escalation to qualified specialists and authorised decision makers.

job.title: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
